title: Custom Task Scheduler Over Native Threading
pattern: Implementing custom thread schedulers, context-switching loops, or timer yield logic on top of operating system threads.
why_bad: It interferes directly with the OS kernel scheduler, wastes CPU clock cycles on active spin waiting, increases tail latency, and defeats standard asynchronous runtime optimizations.
detection: The presence of loop structures containing active spin-locks, thread yields, and microsecond sleep periods to schedule execution.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Embedded bare-metal platforms (`no_std` Rust) or customized high-performance database engines where standard OS schedulers are disabled.
source: Brendan Gregg - _Systems Performance_ Enterprise and the Cloud_ (2013, Pearson Education Limited (US titles)_Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 3 "Operating Systems"; Maurice Herlihy - _The Art of Multiprocessor Programming_ (2008, Morgan Kaufmann), Chapter 12.
